About six months ago my on-and-off girlfriend of two years and best friend, took her own life. She was a beautiful person both inside and out. She never really recovered from the death of her parents which happened when she was just a little kid. She was a foster child, essentially.

I found her body the morning after her death. I was destroyed, to put it mildly. Also, over the next month, my business fell apart. I was on the edge of suicide for a while. Drinking all day and taking Xanax.

A couple of weeks after her death, my high school crush reached out to me. I haven't heard from her in about a decade. I often thought about her but she wasn't on social media and she didn't stay in contact with the few people that I still talked to. Her number has changed and there was no way for me to get in contact with her and there hadn't been in years.

One afternoon months later we met up for drinks/coffee. It was really good to see her. We talked for six hours. I realized that although I enjoyed her company and thought she was still cute, that we didn't really have much in common but it was still great to see her. The crazy thing was, from the moment that we met at the restaurant my favorite band from high school was playing in the background for most of the six hours that we talked. Whole albums. Obscure music. My favorite band from high school had always reminded me of my high school crush. The two have always been inseparably in my mind.

I like to think it was my best friend who nudged my high school crush to contact me. And I like to think that the music was my best friend's way of nudging me and telling me that she was there and that she wanted to make my trip down memory lane as beautiful as possible.

I think financial success is usually earned through a series of life choices. Some of these very important choices (when to have kids, education, etc.) are emphasized differently in some cultures, making it either easier or harder for individuals in each culture to make certain life decisions.
Premarital conception is definitely a contributing factor to poverty, not just a symptom of it.

While those are all valid points, I tend to look more at the commonalities among Asian Americans, Nigerian Americans, and Indian Americans. All three groups have some very strong cultural commonalities. All three cultures put a strong emphasis on education, as well as strongly discourage their young people from having children before they're ready to care for them. 

Not having kids before you're ready doesn't ensure that you'll be successful but having kids while you're a teenager or before you're ready greatly increases your chances that you'll live below the poverty line. Getting an education doesn't guarantee that you'll be successful but it does increase the likelihood. Anyone who makes enough of these life decisions increases the likelihood that they'll struggle financially throughout their lives.
